content.comment_body: Good afternoon, I have set up a heating control program using [product_name] and am encountering difficulties with temperature regulation. The hardware operates correctly with a basic program, so the problem seems to be software-related. My goal is to run two boilers until the temperature reaches 50 degrees, at which point one boiler should turn off while the other continues running until reaching the set temperature. I am unsure which analog function block to use; I tried the threshold block, but it activates in the opposite way than I need. Sequencing works for pumps, but temperature sequencing is problematic. Also, when the temperature drops below 45 degrees, the second boiler should reactivate. I forgot to mention that earlier.
Could you upload your program as a ZIP file?
This additional information might help clarify the solution.
Thank you. I'm unfamiliar with the amplified function block but will try to learn more about it.
The "analog amplifier" block isn't strictly required. However, I usually use it out of habit.
Have you been able to resolve the problem?

analysis.insight_summary: Forum members are discussing temperature control logic with [product_name], focusing on managing two boilers with specific temperature thresholds. The main challenge involves choosing the correct analog function block for switching boilers as temperatures change. The main user reports that the threshold block doesn't yield the expected result, causing confusion over accurate function block usage for temperature-based sequencing.
analysis.user_expectations: The user expects the software to feature clear and user-friendly analog function blocks to facilitate temperature control logic. They anticipate being able to set thresholds logically for sequential activation and deactivation of devices, along with accessible documentation or guidance within the software for selecting and applying these function blocks.
